text: What we do have is an annual planning cycle basically, we call investment plans and it's for fairly large SWOTs to the organization.
speaker: Brandon Chu
context: Lenny asks about Shopify's framework or process for making bigger decisions. Brandon explains their annual planning cycle where VPs create investment plans for large portions of the organization. Each investment plan covers about 20% of Shopify's workforce under a VP and outlines what that team will accomplish that year, whether through directional changes or specific outcomes.
text_ko: 우리에게는 연간 계획 주기(annual planning cycle)가 있어요. 보통 '투자 계획'(investment plans)이라고 부르는데, 조직에 꽤 큰 영향을 미치는 규모의 SWOT(강점·약점·기회·위협, Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats) 관련 결정이에요.
text_zh: 我们现在有的是一个年度规划流程，基本上我们叫投资计划(investment plans)，主要是针对公司比较大的SWOT分析。
text_es: Lo que sí tenemos es básicamente un ciclo de planificación anual, le decimos planes de inversión y es para análisis FODA (SWOTs) bastante grandes para la organización.
key_sentence: We call investment plans for fairly large SWOTs consolidated under a VP.
original_text: What we do have is an annual planning cycle basically, we call investment plans and it's for fairly large SWOTs to the organization. I'm talking like 20% chunks of all of Shopify consolidated under a VP here and there to put forward a vision for what that team's going to accomplish that year, whether that is a directional change or even specific outcomes in some cases.

vocabulary.definition: A systematic process that organizations follow each year to set goals, allocate resources, and develop strategies for the upcoming year.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, the annual planning cycle is crucial for aligning departmental objectives with overall company goals and ensuring that resources are effectively utilized.
vocabulary.nuance: This term implies a recurring, structured approach to planning, which can be contrasted with more ad-hoc or reactive planning methods.

vocabulary.definition: Documents or strategies outlining how an organization intends to allocate financial resources to achieve specific objectives or returns.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and businesses, investment plans are critical for attracting investors and guiding financial decision-making to maximize growth and profitability.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often carries a connotation of careful analysis and forecasting, distinguishing it from more casual or informal financial strategies.

vocabulary.definition: A structured group of individuals working together to achieve common goals, often characterized by defined roles, responsibilities, and hierarchies.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, the term organization refers not only to companies but also to non-profits and other entities that require coordination and management to function effectively.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a formal structure, but it can also refer to informal groups or networks, depending on the context.

text: But what's really amazing and also difficult about Shopify though is we're pretty good at never falling into sunk-cost fallacy. So we'll throw it all away anytime if the world changes.
speaker: Brandon Chu
context: Brandon continues explaining Shopify's decision-making approach, highlighting how they avoid the sunk-cost fallacy. Sunk-cost fallacy is when people continue investing in something because they've already spent resources on it, even when it's no longer the best option. He explains that Shopify is willing to abandon projects even after months of work if circumstances change, which can be challenging for employees but keeps the company agile.
text_ko: 그런데 Shopify에서 정말 놀랍기도 하고 어려운 점은, 저희가 매몰비용 오류(sunk-cost fallacy)에 거의 빠지지 않는다는 거예요. 세상이 바뀌면 언제든지 전부 다 버려요.
text_zh: 不过Shopify真正厉害但也很难做到的一点是，我们从来不会陷入沉没成本谬误(sunk-cost fallacy)。所以只要外界有变化，我们随时都敢把之前的东西全部推倒重来。
text_es: Pero lo que es realmente increíble y también complicado de Shopify es que somos bastante buenos para no caer en esa trampa de "ya invertimos mucho, hay que seguir". Así que estamos dispuestos a tirar todo por la borda cuando sea necesario si el mundo cambia.
key_sentence: Shopify avoids the sunk-cost fallacy, throwing it all away if the world changes.
original_text: But what's really amazing and also difficult about Shopify though is we're pretty good at never falling into sunk-cost fallacy. So we'll throw it all away anytime if the world changes. And so that's why it's actually a really tricky place for a lot of folks because there are cases and it's happened to me many times where it's just like you're building three, six months into something and it's just not important anymore or the world changed.

vocabulary.definition: The sunk-cost fallacy is a cognitive bias that occurs when individuals continue an endeavor, or continue consuming or pursuing an option, based on previously invested resources (time, money, or effort) rather than current and future benefits.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and startup environments, recognizing the sunk-cost fallacy can prevent companies from making poor decisions based on past investments, allowing them to pivot or abandon projects that no longer align with strategic goals.
vocabulary.nuance: While it is important to acknowledge past investments, it is crucial to focus on future potential rather than being anchored by previous costs.

text: I think what I learned over the arc of my career is that especially when it comes to product management specifically, it's a lot of the hard skills that PMs are known for, so organizational, analytical, good communication, even technical skills.
speaker: Brandon Chu
context: Lenny asks Brandon for advice on what helped him achieve his impressive career trajectory at Shopify that newer PMs could learn from. Brandon explains that traditional PM hard skills like organization, analysis, and communication are just the baseline requirements for entry-level PM roles. He's setting up to explain what skills are needed to advance beyond that level.
text_ko: 제 경험상, 특히 프로덕트 매니지먼트(product management) 분야에서는 PM들(PMs)이 잘 알려진 하드 스킬(hard skills)—조직력, 분석력, 의사소통 능력, 심지어 기술적 역량 같은 것들이 훨씬 더 중요하다는 걸 배웠어요.
text_zh: 我觉得在我整个职业生涯中学到的是，特别是在产品管理(product management)这块，很大程度上还是要靠产品经理(PM)应该具备的那些硬技能，比如组织能力、分析能力、沟通能力，甚至技术能力。
text_es: Creo que lo que he aprendido a lo largo de mi carrera es que, especialmente en product management (gestión de producto), se trata mucho de las habilidades técnicas por las que los PMs son conocidos: organización, análisis, buena comunicación, e incluso habilidades técnicas.
key_sentence: Table stakes for PMs include organizational, analytical, and communication skills.
original_text: I think what I learned over the arc of my career is that especially when it comes to product management specifically, it's a lot of the hard skills that PMs are known for, so organizational, analytical, good communication, even technical skills. There's sort of table stakes and commodities to be an entry level PM.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to the ability to analyze information, break it down into components, and understand its structure.
vocabulary.businessContext: Analytical skills are crucial in business for making data-driven decisions, evaluating market trends, and optimizing processes.
vocabulary.nuance: While analytical often has a positive connotation in problem-solving contexts, it can suggest a lack of creativity if overemphasized.

vocabulary.definition: Pertaining to the arrangement and coordination of resources, tasks, and personnel to achieve specific goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: Organizational skills are essential for effective project management, ensuring that teams work efficiently and deadlines are met.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a systematic approach, but overemphasis on organization may stifle flexibility and creativity.

vocabulary.definition: The act of conveying information effectively through various means, including verbal, written, and non-verbal methods.
vocabulary.businessContext: Effective communication is vital in business for collaboration, stakeholder engagement, and ensuring that all team members are aligned with company objectives.
vocabulary.nuance: While communication is generally viewed positively, it can also imply challenges when miscommunication occurs or when messages are unclear.

text: But I think ultimately to have the highest trajectory and what certainly was a tailwind for my career was you guys have to lean into those founder skills.
speaker: Brandon Chu
context: Brandon continues his advice about advancing as a PM beyond entry-level skills. He identifies 'founder skills' as the key differentiator for high career trajectory. These include storytelling abilities, getting the best performance from team members, fostering creativity and motivation, and making difficult decisions with strong conviction even when there's no clear analytical solution.
text_ko: 하지만 결국 가장 높은 성장 궤적(trajectory)을 얻으려면 — 그리고 제 커리어에 확실한 순풍(tailwind)이 되어준 건 — 여러분이 그런 창업가 역량(founder skills)을 적극적으로 받아들이고 활용하는 거예요.
text_zh: 但我觉得要想有最好的发展轨迹，对我职业生涯帮助最大的，就是你们一定要发挥好那些创始人技能(founder skills)。
text_es: Pero al final, para tener la mejor trayectoria y lo que definitivamente me ayudó mucho en mi carrera fue que tienes que apostar fuerte por esas habilidades de fundador (founder skills).
key_sentence: Lean into founder skills for the highest trajectory and high conviction decisions.
original_text: But I think ultimately to have the highest trajectory and what certainly was a tailwind for my career was you guys have to lean into those founder skills. And so things like being a great storyteller, how to get the most out of people around you, foster creative and motivated teams and know how to make really, really hard high conviction decisions that actually can't be solved.

vocabulary.definition: The path or progression of an individual's career or a project's development over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, trajectory often refers to the expected growth or success of a company, product, or individual based on current performance and market conditions.
vocabulary.nuance: While trajectory typically has a positive connotation, it can also imply a downward trend if used in a negative context.

vocabulary.definition: A favorable condition or support that aids progress or success.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups, a tailwind might refer to market trends or external factors that positively influence a company's growth potential.
vocabulary.nuance: Tailwind suggests an advantage that is somewhat external and not solely dependent on the individual's or company's efforts.

vocabulary.definition: To embrace or actively engage with a particular skill, idea, or situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, leaning into skills means recognizing and utilizing one's strengths to drive success or innovation.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase conveys a proactive approach, suggesting that one should not shy away from challenges but rather confront them head-on.

vocabulary.definition: A set of competencies and attributes that are essential for starting and running a successful business, often including leadership, vision, and resilience.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup ecosystem, founder skills are critical for navigating challenges, securing funding, and building a strong team and company culture.
vocabulary.nuance: The term implies a blend of both hard and soft skills, emphasizing the unique abilities that distinguish successful entrepreneurs from others.

text: Oh, it's honestly been the most important thing I've ever done in my career unbelievably. And it's had probably two really interesting effects.
speaker: Brandon Chu
context: Lenny asks Brandon about the impact writing has had on his career. Brandon describes writing as the single most important thing for his career success. He explains that during Shopify's rapid growth phase (hyperscale), new employees were joining constantly - he uses the vivid expression 'people are falling from the sky' to describe how quickly new hires were arriving and needing onboarding and context.
text_ko: 솔직히 제 경력에서 해온 일 중 가장 중요한 일이었어요. 믿기 어려울 정도예요. 그리고 그게 아마도 두 가지 정말 흥미로운 효과를 가져왔어요.
text_zh: 说实话，这绝对是我职业生涯中做过的最重要的事情，真的没想到会这样。而且带来了两个特别有意思的影响。
text_es: Oye, honestamente ha sido lo más importante que he hecho en mi carrera profesional, increíblemente. Y me parece que ha tenido como dos efectos súper interesantes.
key_sentence: it's honestly been the most important thing I've ever done in my career unbelievably.
original_text: Oh, it's honestly been the most important thing I've ever done in my career unbelievably. And it's had probably two really interesting effects. One is that as Shopify grew and when we were going through hyperscale, you probably recognize this from your Airbnb days as well but people are falling from the sky.

vocabulary.definition: Of great significance or value; having a major effect on a situation or outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the corporate world, 'important' is frequently used to prioritize tasks, projects, or decisions that significantly affect business objectives or strategies.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can sometimes be subjective, as what is considered 'important' may vary between individuals or organizations.

text: writing externally and getting momentum externally was a better way to influence internally... Tobi would read my post... and he'd be like, 'Great post.' And I'd be like, 'Hey, daddy loves me.
speaker: Brandon Chu
context: Brandon explains how his external writing helped him gain influence within Shopify's chaotic, fast-growing environment. With so much happening internally, it was difficult to get the attention of 200+ PMs for new ideas. He discovered that publishing content externally and gaining traction outside the company was more effective for influencing internal decisions. When Tobi (Shopify's CEO) would praise his posts, it built his credibility and trust within the organization.
text_ko: 외부에 글을 쓰고 외부에서 모멘텀(momentum)을 얻는 게 내부에서 영향력을 행사하는 더 좋은 방법이었어요... 토비가 제 글을 읽고 "좋은 글이네요"라고 하면 저는 "아, 아빠가 날 사랑하네요" 하고 좋아하곤 했어요.
text_zh: 对外发声、在外面造势，反而是影响内部的更好方式...Tobi会看我的文章...然后他会说"写得不错"，我就会想"哎呀，老板认可我了"。
text_es: escribir para afuera y generar tracción externamente era mejor forma de influir internamente... Tobi leía mi post... y me decía 'Excelente post.' Y yo pensaba, 'Ey, papi me quiere.'
key_sentence: writing externally and getting momentum externally was a better way to influence internally
original_text: So I actually found that writing externally and getting momentum externally was a better way to influence internally what was happening, to the effect that Tobi would read my post here and there and he'd be like, 'Great post.' And I'd be like, 'Hey, daddy loves me.'

vocabulary.definition: Momentum refers to the force or speed of movement gained by a process or course of events. In a business context, it often describes the increasing growth or progress of a project or initiative.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and startups, momentum can indicate the accelerating success of a product launch or the growing interest in a company's services, often leading to increased investment and market share.
vocabulary.nuance: While momentum typically has a positive connotation, it can also imply a sense of urgency that may lead to hasty decisions if not managed carefully.

vocabulary.definition: Influence is the capacity to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of someone or something. It often involves persuasion or the ability to shape opinions and decisions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, influence is crucial for leadership, marketing strategies, and stakeholder engagement, as it can determine how effectively ideas are communicated and adopted within an organization.
vocabulary.nuance: Influence can carry both positive and negative connotations; it is essential to use it ethically to foster trust and collaboration.

text: Do a legitimate side hustle, found a company on the side and learn everything else. Because I think sometimes you're in this silo of your feature, your area or whatnot.
speaker: Brandon Chu
context: Lenny asks Brandon for one piece of advice for PMs to level up in their careers. Brandon recommends starting a legitimate side business or founding a company while working as a PM. He explains that PMs often get trapped in a narrow focus on their specific feature or product area, missing the broader perspective of what it takes to build and run a complete business.
text_ko: 정말 제대로 된 사이드 허슬(side hustle)을 해보거나 부업으로 회사를 하나 창업해서 다른 모든 걸 배워보세요. 가끔은 자기 담당 기능이나 영역에만 갇혀 있는 경우가 있다고 생각해요.
text_zh: 搞个正经的副业，在业余时间创个公司，然后学学其他方面的东西。因为我觉得有时候你就被困在自己那个功能模块里，或者说你那个小圈子里。
text_es: Busca un trabajo extra que sea legítimo, monta una empresa por tu cuenta y aprende todo lo demás. Porque creo que a veces te quedas metido en tu burbuja, en tu área o lo que sea.
key_sentence: Do a legitimate side hustle to avoid being in this silo as a PM.
original_text: Everyone has so many different backgrounds, but I'd say overall, based on most PMs that I've met, I'd say, look, it is hard to do when you are a PM somewhere, but do a legitimate side hustle, found a company on the side and learn everything else. Because I think sometimes you're in this silo of your feature, your area or whatnot.

vocabulary.definition: Conforming to the law or to rules; valid and acceptable.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'legitimate' often refers to practices or operations that are lawful and ethically sound, distinguishing them from fraudulent or unethical activities.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'legitimate' generally has a positive connotation, it can imply that something is being questioned or scrutinized for its authenticity.

vocabulary.definition: A system, process, or department that operates in isolation from others, often leading to a lack of communication and collaboration.
vocabulary.businessContext: In organizational settings, silos can hinder innovation and efficiency, as teams may not share information or resources effectively.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting inefficiency and a need for greater integration within an organization.

vocabulary.definition: To establish or set up an organization, institution, or company.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup ecosystem, 'found' is commonly used to describe the act of starting a new business venture, often involving innovation and entrepreneurship.
vocabulary.nuance: The term implies a sense of initiative and leadership, often associated with risk-taking and vision.
